# Git worktrees and auto-land

<!-- practices:learn:start (generated by scripts/practices/practices.py; do not edit) -->
**Learn this:** [Landing claims](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/landing-claims/index.html) (explainer with a [quiz](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/landing-claims/index.html#quiz)); [Worktrees and landing](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/worktrees-and-landing/index.html) (explainer with a [quiz](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/worktrees-and-landing/index.html#quiz)). Learner path: Working with agents, step 1.

A workflow for one maintainer with several agents working in parallel.

## Isolation

- Never edit or commit on `main`. Each task gets a branch in its own worktree.
- Keep worktrees inside the clone (`.worktrees/<short-name>` or `.claude/worktrees/<short-name>`, gitignored:
  [Where worktrees live](#where-worktrees-live)). IDEs
  and agent sandboxes trust the workspace root; sibling `../x` checkouts trigger
  permission prompts. HQ's command guard denies `git worktree add` with a path outside the repo (allowed: a relative
  path, `~/dev/hq/`, the session scratchpad, `~/.cache/hq-measure/`): cleanup, status and conformance checks look only
  inside the repos.

```bash
git fetch origin
git worktree add -b feat/<short> .worktrees/<short> origin/main
```

- Branch prefixes: `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `test/`; short kebab-case.
- One worktree per independent task; never two agents on the same files.

## Fan-out sizing and conflicts

Generated-file conflicts, landing queues and the tiered gate: [parallel-work-and-landing.md](parallel-work-and-landing.md).

- **Conflicts are prevented, not resolved.** Give each worker its own files; the plan lists the files per unit before
  anyone starts, and two units that touch the same file become one unit or run one after the other. Worktrees isolate
  the writes, not the merge: the vendor docs offer no conflict-resolution procedure, only this prevention.
- **At most 3 workers per repo at once** (HQ's `/fleet` cap). The source's nearest statement is that three focused
  teammates often do better than five scattered ones; the number 3 is ours, set by review and gate capacity, not
  by a vendor figure.
- **Untracked config does not follow into a worktree.** A fresh worktree has no gitignored files such as `.env`. List
  the small ones in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the repo root (`.gitignore` syntax; only files that match a pattern
  and are also gitignored are copied, so tracked files are never duplicated; it covers `--worktree`, subagent and
  desktop-app worktrees, but is not processed when a `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces creation, so copy inside the
  hook) and symlink large directories (`node_modules`, build caches) instead of copying.
- **Migration playbook** (our shape; Claude Code's `/batch` skill does the same: 5 to 30 independent units, a plan you approve, then one
  background subagent per unit in its own worktree, each opening a PR or reporting back): 1. one plan
  with the unit list and the files per unit, 2. approval of that plan, 3. one worktree and branch per unit, 4. one gate
  per unit, 5. land one branch at a time, pull and re-run the fast check between landings
  ([retiring-the-old-stack.md](retiring-the-old-stack.md#running-agents-in-parallel)). Do not fan out work that shares
  files or context ([subagents-and-context.md](subagents-and-context.md#hub-and-spoke-or-peer-mesh)).

## Push every commit

Every commit is pushed right away (WIP included) to the work branch, so
progress survives a dead machine or container. `main` gets work only when it is
finished. Never leave local `main` ahead of `origin/main`.

## Auto-land by default

When the task is done and the full gate passed, the agent lands without asking:

1. `git fetch origin`, merge `origin/main` into the work branch (merge, not
   rebase, unless asked; merging keeps pushed history intact).
2. In the primary checkout: `git checkout main && git pull`, merge the work
   branch, `git push origin main`. When the primary checkout holds other
   sessions' uncommitted work, push from the worktree instead
   (`git push origin HEAD:main`), then still update the primary checkout:
   `git -C <primary> pull --ff-only`. Its dev servers serve those files, so
   skipping this leaves the running app stale. Never stash or reset there; if
   the fast-forward is refused, report it.
3. Remove the worktree, delete the merged branch locally and on the remote.
4. Report the commit subject + short SHA and which checks ran.

If the push is rejected because another agent landed first: fetch, merge again,
re-run the checks the new commits affect, retry.

Land only the tree that passed. The gate runs for minutes and `main` moves meanwhile: fetch right before the merge and
check `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`. If it fails, merge again and re-gate; a landing that pulled in
commits nobody gated is a guess, and the only fix is a gate on `main` afterwards (observed once: the check passed, but
only after the push).

Only a full gate result lands a branch, never a local spot check: a tool missing in the agent's shell (shellcheck was not
on its PATH) means run the gate, which has it, not skip the check. A landing before the gate's last verdict puts a
rejected commit on `main` (Optiomni, 2026-11-04: `just repos-land` landed a script that failed shellcheck, a follow-up
had to land). Run one gate per worktree at a time. A branch that is behind `main` shows the newer main files as deleted
in `git diff --stat origin/main`: merge `origin/main` before judging a diff or gating.

### A shared install symlink stays untracked

A worktree's `node_modules` symlink (made to share the install) must stay untracked. A builder that runs `git add -A`
commits it, and a worktree with the untracked symlink makes `repos-land` print "NOT finished": check
`git ls-files web/node_modules` on a builder's branch, `git rm --cached` it, and remove the symlink before
`repos-finish`.

Prevent it in the repo: ignore the link with a pattern without a trailing slash (`node_modules`, not
`node_modules/`; a slash matches directories only, never a symlink), and tell builders to stage files by name. If a
tracked link does land, merging it replaces the primary clone's real `node_modules` with a link to itself (Optiomni,
2026-11-04: every tool in the primary clone broke): remove the link, reinstall (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
--prefer-offline`), `git rm --cached` the link in a follow-up and run `git update-index --force-remove` in the primary
before pulling it.

A background gate's "completed" notice means the launcher exited, not that the gate passed: read the result
(`hq q-gate-result`) and treat `RUNNING` as not done. A builder that reports PASS before the result line exists
is wrong until the line says so (seen twice with Sonnet builders, 2026-11-04).

A merge conflict in a generated file (API revision counter and hash, schema, a version fixture) is never merged by
hand: take the other side, run the generator, commit the result. Formatters that run as the gate's first stage can
rewrite files and leave the pass unrecorded ("uncommitted changes"): commit the rewrite and run the gate once more.

## When to stop and ask instead

Show a numbered menu (PR / merge / push branch only / stop) when:

- the user asked to review first, asked for a PR, or said "don't land";
- the gate failed, was skipped, or a flaky test could not be confirmed;
- merging `main` needed non-trivial conflict resolution;
- the change is hard to undo or reaches outside the repo: data migrations or
  deletions, secrets, CI/deploy config, major dependency bumps, force pushes;
- the result only partly does what was asked, or contains a judgment call.

A numbered menu lets the user answer with one character from a phone.

**Split before asking.** When only some files of a branch hit the list (a CI workflow, deploy config), do not hold the
whole branch: put those files on a branch of their own, land the rest by the normal rules, and ask only about the split-off
part. Done at the start (separate commits, ideally separate branches) it costs nothing; discovered at landing it costs a
round trip of the maintainer's time. The agent brief says which files are outward-facing so the worker splits them.

When stopping, end the reply with a run command from the **feature worktree**
(`cd <repo>/.worktrees/<short> && <run>`) so the user can try the change; never
point at the primary checkout for unmerged work. After landing, give the run
command from the **primary** checkout instead. Then the menu:

```text
Ready to land — reply with a number:
1. Commit + merge latest main into work branch + push + open PR (leave open)
2. Commit + merge latest main into work branch + merge into main + update primary checkout + clean worktree
3. Commit + push the work branch only (no merge, no PR)
4. Stop (leave uncommitted / unpushed as-is)
```

Do nothing (no commit, push, PR, merge) until the user replies.

| Reply | Agent does |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | commit, fetch, merge `origin/main`, push the branch, `gh pr create`, report the URL; then update local `main` in the primary checkout (does not merge the PR) |
| 2 | commit, fetch, merge `origin/main`, merge into `main` in the primary checkout, push, remove the worktree, delete the branch; no PR |
| 3 | commit and push the work branch; no merge of main, no PR |
| 4 | nothing further |

Synonyms count: "PR" / "open PR" = 1; "merge" / "ship it" / "merge and clean" = 2;
"commit only" = 3; "stop" / "don't land" = 4. Without `gh`, option 1 pushes the
branch and gives the GitHub compare URL.

Docs-only changes need just the pre-commit hooks on the changed files, not the
full gate.

Narrow exceptions: read-only questions need no branch; "commit on this branch"
means 3; a full custom git sequence from the user wins over auto-land and the
menu.

Where a land on `main` would redeploy a live service, deploy from a fast-forward-only `prod` branch instead, so
auto-land stays safe: [releases-and-versions.md](releases-and-versions.md#a-prod-branch-for-auto-deployed-services).

Production hosts: if a dev machine doubles as production, restarts and
env/compose edits there are production changes; treat them as risky and use the
menu, not auto-land.

## Commit messages

- Conventional Commits: `type(scope): lowercase subject`; types `feat`, `fix`,
  `docs`, `test`, `chore`, `style`; scope optional (`feat(web): …`).
- The body says what changed and why, when the subject is not enough, and how it was checked (the test,
  the command, the page looked at): [change-discipline.md](change-discipline.md#commits).
- Merges of main read `Merge origin/main into <branch>`.
- Agent commits end with the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer for the model.
- Trailers are provenance, not authority. `Co-Authored-By:` and `Claude-Session:` come from the harness and name the
  model family and the session. `Agent:`, `Machine:`, `Model:`, `Flow:` (from `just docs-trace trailers`, set only
  when `HQ_HANDLE` is) say which worker, on which machine, under which flow version. `Request:` / `Item:` tie the commit
  to its ask. The shared git author stays `land-batch`; none of these marks grants rights. `just docs-trace <sha>`
  shows them with the ship row and gate log. Never put names, emails or secrets in a trailer: handles only.

## Housekeeping

- After each land (and at session start) delete agent branches already merged
  into `origin/main` and prune stale worktrees; list unmerged old ones to the
  user instead of deleting them. A `git-cleanup` recipe with `--dry-run` makes
  this safe to run often.

## Before removing a worktree

The gate's fixers (rustfmt, prettier, whitespace) can rewrite files after the last commit. Run `git status` after the
gate and commit those changes before `git worktree remove`; `--force` silently throws them away, and the landed commit
is then unformatted. A gate that fails with timeouts in many unrelated specs ran under machine load: wait for the
machine (`machine-wait`), then re-run; do not touch the specs.

## Verify a worker's "landed"

A worker's "landed on main" can mean only the local `main` of the shared checkout while `origin/main` has moved
(`git status -sb` shows `ahead 1, behind 1`: diverged). The supervisor does not take the word:

1. `git fetch && git status -sb` and `git log origin/main` in the checkout: is the sha on `origin/main`?
2. If diverged: merge `origin/main` into the landing's work branch in its worktree (merge, as in the landing steps
   above; never rebase, reset or stash the main checkout), re-run the gate once (the tree changed), push, then
   `git pull --ff-only` in the main checkout so it matches (a refused fast-forward is reported).
3. A worker that fixed a gate failure *after* its gate run says so: "gate not re-run after this fix". The supervisor
   then re-runs the gate before accepting; a hand-back without that sentence is read as "gate ran on this exact tree".

Prepared check: `just repos-landed <repo> <sha>` ([prepared-commands.md](prepared-commands.md)).

## Skipping a re-run of the gate

Record a pass per git *tree* (not commit) in the shared git dir
(`$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/quality-passed/<tree>`). A merge that
produces an already-passed tree, or differs only in docs, needs no new gate.
See [quality-gate.md](quality-gate.md).

## Where worktrees live

**Rule.** A worktree of repo X lives inside X's own clone, in a hidden, gitignored folder: `.claude/worktrees/<name>`
(what Claude Code creates and the only place `EnterWorktree` enters without a prompt) or `.worktrees/<name>` (made by
hand or by a script). Never a sibling folder (`~/dev/x-wt/<name>`), never a visible `worktrees/`, never inside another
repo's tree. A session starts in the main checkout (or with `claude --worktree <name>`) and works in a worktree below
it; workers never edit the main checkout.

| Concern | Inside the clone (hidden, ignored) | Sibling folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code reads and edits | under the start directory: no prompt | outside it: a `Read(//…/**)` prompt per folder, or `--add-dir` |
| `EnterWorktree`, resume, the periodic sweep | built for `.claude/worktrees/` | approval prompt that no rule turns off |
| Saved approvals, plugins, project skills | shared through the main checkout | shared too (same repository) |
| `git status`, ripgrep, prek discovery | skipped: ignored and dot-prefixed | not seen at all |
| HQ storage, cleanup, watch, keeper, guard | found by path (`/.claude/worktrees/`, `/.worktrees/`) | invisible: piles up |
| Container or sandbox mount | one mount of the clone covers worktree and `.git` | two mounts at the same absolute paths |
| Tools that ignore `.gitignore` (`grep -r`, `find`, `du`, an IDE index) | see every copy: exclude the folder | clean |

- **Hidden and ignored, both.** A visible `worktrees/<name>` broke every commit in the main checkout: prek found the
  worktree's own config as a nested project. prek skips dot-prefixed and ignored folders, but caches the discovery
  (`--refresh`). The ignore pattern is `.claude/worktrees/` and `.worktrees/` in the tracked `.gitignore`, not
  `.git/info/exclude` (per clone, so a new machine would lack it).
- **Another machine.** Each machine has its own clone and its own worktrees below it; git links them by absolute path
  (`git worktree repair` after a moved clone). Never on a network share or synced folder. The tmux launcher starts a
  session in the main checkout of the repo `-C` names, also when `-C` is a worktree: pass `--worktree <name>` as a
  Claude argument, or let the worker create its worktree.
- **Cargo.** A worktree under another repo's tree sits in that repo's workspace discovery and `cargo` fails: X's
  worktree goes inside X. Each linked worktree builds into its own `target/`
  ([rust-build-times.md](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/rust-build-times.md)), which storage and cleanup find only below the clone.
- **Exceptions.** Script-owned temporary worktrees that the script removes itself (a landing or ship trial under
  `$TMPDIR` or `~/.local/state/hq/ships/`), measurement copies in `~/.cache/hq-measure/` and the session scratchpad. A
  sibling that cannot be avoided is added with `--add-dir` (file access; a settings `additionalDirectories` entry
  loads no configuration from it) and gets a backlog item for its removal.

## A repo rule must not make every landing wait for the maintainer

A repo's `AGENTS.md` should allow landing by default: merge into the default branch and push once the full gate passed
(the "Auto-land by default" steps above). A line such as "do not push without the maintainer's decision" turns every
finished branch into a wait; in one repo (2026-11-08) five green branches sat unmerged for a day, and a trial merge of
them found a compile error that only the combined tree showed (a struct field added on one branch, a constructor
rewritten on another). Waiting also lets branches drift apart.

- Write the rule as the exception list from "When to stop and ask instead", not as a blanket approval. A repo may add
  its own exceptions (a shared remote with other committers, a paper whose numbers must not change), each with the
  reason and the check that replaces the approval (a PR, a reproducibility hash).
- Several ready branches: trial-merge them in a scratch worktree in dependency order, fix conflicts there (a compile
  error with no text conflict is common), run the full gate on the result, push it as an integration branch, then
  fast-forward main.
- Branch pushes are always fine; only the push of main to a shared remote needs the exception to be named.

- Observed in a managed repo's logo landings (2026-11-07): a local-only "landed" with `main` diverged from origin, and a

  <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-status>; `git pull --rebase`: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull>.
- Observed in HQ's backlog v2 work (2026-11-03): a worktree under HQ's `.claude/worktrees/` broke cargo for a
  second Rust repo.
- Observed in the JAS Bot passkey landing (2026-11-01): a generated-file conflict, a formatter rewrite after the gate
  and a `main` that moved during a seven-minute gate.
- Observed in Optiomni's family tree and icon landings (2026-11-04): a landing before the gate verdict, a committed
  `node_modules` symlink, a branch behind `main` read as deleted files.
- Optiomni's online play landings (2026-11-04): the tracked link replaced the primary clone's `node_modules`; gitignore
  semantics for a trailing slash: <https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore> ("If there is a separator at the end of the pattern then the pattern will only match directories").
- `git worktree add -b`, linked worktrees, `remove`, `prune`: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree>
- `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (the shared git dir for the gate-pass records): <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse>
- Commit message format `type(scope): description`, body and footers: <https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/>
- Observed in HQ's own repos and sessions (auto-land, push-every-commit, the numbered menu); no external source for
  those workflow rules.
- `claude --worktree <name>`, `.worktreeinclude` (`.gitignore` syntax, gitignored matches only, skipped under a
  `WorktreeCreate` hook), `worktree.baseRef`, the `/batch` mention (runs outside git only with a `WorktreeCreate` hook)
  (read 2026-11-07, full page): <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees>. The `/batch` figures (5 to 30 units, plan
  approval, a worktree per unit, a git repo or `WorktreeCreate` hook needed) are in the commands reference (read
  2026-11-07): <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands>.
- "Three focused teammates often outperform five scattered ones", own files per teammate (read 2026-11-07):
  <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams>
- Where worktrees live (read 2026-11-15). Verified in the vendor docs: worktrees are created under
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` with the tip to gitignore it; `EnterWorktree` outside that folder asks for approval that
  a rule or "don't ask again" does not suppress; resume, the subagent sweep and saved approvals (kept in the main
  checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`, valid in every worktree) are described for that location; a background
  session may edit "in a worktree made with `git worktree add` under the directory the session started in"; a
  sibling path is shown only under "Manage worktrees manually": <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees>. Reads
  need no approval "within the working directory and additional directories", a `cd` outside them saves a Read rule
  for that path, `--add-dir` and `additionalDirectories` (the settings key grants file access only):
  <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions>.
- git: the path of `git worktree add` is free (the manual's example is `../hotfix`), links are absolute unless
  `worktree.useRelativePaths`, `repair` after a move, `lock` for a worktree on a share that is not always mounted;
  the manual says nothing on nesting or ignoring: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree>.
- prek workspace discovery skips dot-prefixed folders, respects `.gitignore` and `.prekignore`, and is cached
  (`--refresh`) (search summary, the page itself did not load): <https://prek.j178.dev/workspace/>.
- Observed in HQ: sibling `~/dev/hq-wt-*` folders that no cleanup or status check saw (2026-11-08), a visible
  `worktrees/` that broke main-checkout commits (2026-11-11), and workers in `~/dev/hq-wt/<name>` on a second machine
  (2026-11-15: a `Read(//…/hq-wt/<name>/**)` prompt per worker, and the tmux launcher started in the main checkout).
  Our inference, not a vendor statement: the table's container, IDE and "piles up" rows, and that the launcher should
  stay in the main checkout.
